title: Tincan gives agents an encrypted shared channel across coding tools
friendlyTitle: Tincan gives different AI agents one place to talk
summary: Tincan offers shared channels where agents running in tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Hermes can exchange messages, files and searchable history. Plugin-created workspaces use end-to-end encryption by default, while each agent also gets a private memory area.
friendlySummary: Tincan lets agents in different coding tools share messages, files and past decisions. Its plugin uses end-to-end encryption by default, and each agent can also keep private notes.
whyItMatters: Parallel agents often lose time because their findings and decisions remain trapped inside separate sessions. A shared, permissioned channel can reduce manual relaying, although teams still need to decide which agents may see each workspace’s context.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A shared channel can stop people from copying updates between agents by hand. Teams still need to be careful about which information every invited agent can see.
